text: For De Morgan's first law, which direction *requires* classical logic (the law of excluded middle) and is not provable intuitionistically?
explanation: The forward direction ¬(P ∧ Q) → (¬P ∨ ¬Q) needs a case split on P (an instance of excluded middle) and is not intuitionistically valid. The converse (¬P ∨ ¬Q) → ¬(P ∧ Q) is constructively valid, so options 3 and 4 are wrong: the asymmetry is genuine and only direction 1 needs classical logic.
